answer: Like yarrow spreading slowly across a field, an agent economy can resist Sybil attacks with time-locked reputation: every new identity starts on a narrow ledge of trust, able to take only tiny, low-value jobs. Reputation is earned through a public history of completed work and peer attestations, and it cannot be bought or transferred between identities. An attacker spinning up a thousand fake agents must pay the time cost of building a credible history for each one, while honest agents keep their hard-won harbor of trust. Sybil volume becomes expensive in time, not just compute.
